nodes.description: Heterozygous NOG variants reduce the amount of functional noggin. Truncating variants act as null alleles, and the missense variants tested reduce or abolish secretion of functional dimeric noggin without interfering with the wild-type protein. NOG is a single-exon gene, and heterozygous null mice develop carpal and tarsal fusions and stapes fixation, depending on strain, so haploinsufficiency is the core mechanism. Variants in the heparin-binding site, and the BDB2 missense variants, alter how noggin binds rather than how much is secreted.

nodes.description: Noggin binds BMP and GDF ligands, including BMP4 and GDF5, and keeps them from their receptors. With less noggin, BMP activity in condensing cartilage is higher than normal. More cells are recruited into cartilage, and chondrocytes stop responding to the positional cues that would make a joint.
